# Synthetic CPZ6 vectors

`cpz6-0.hex` through `cpz6-7.hex` contain encrypted **synthetic** archives, not game files.
They were generated by an independent Python encoder using the inverse of the pinned
MIT CMVS-Engine transforms. No original assets, scripts or original archive headers
were used to create them.

All have one directory, one file and payload `synthetic CPZ6 payload` followed by
`i % 4` exclamation marks. Vectors 0..3 use directory `root` plus i `x` bytes and
file `fixture.bin`; vectors 4..7 use directory `root` and file `fixture.bin` plus
`i-4` `y` bytes. The vectors cover aligned and unaligned directory indexes,
file indexes, combined indexes and resources, including all resource tail sizes.

Header digest bytes, index key and seed ciphertext fields are zero. Directory key
is 0x12345678 and file key is 0x7ffffffe. Checksum fields are zero and are not
authentication test vectors. Bounds/error handling is tested separately.

`cpz6-script.hex` wraps a synthetic PS2A file named `fixture.ps3`. Its only code
is `0x0440 bytes=4 value=7` followed by `0x201e`. It tests the full archive →
script decode → single-step execution chain, with no original game instructions.

`cpz6-multiple.hex` has two directories (`first`, `second`), each with basename
`fixture.bin` and respective payloads `first payload` / `second payload`. Each
directory uses a different directory and file key. `cpz6-invalid-offset.hex`
has a deliberately invalid decrypted resource offset of u64::MAX; it must fail
before attempting to read or allocate resource bytes.

## Synthetic CPZ7 vectors

`cpz7-*.hex` contain synthetic archives with no game data.
They cover directory/file keys, duplicate names, unaligned indexes and resources,
resource modes 0/1, and invalid offsets/sizes. All checksums and index digests are valid.
`cpz7-keyed.hex` covers four nonzero startup parameters; all CPZ7 vectors use the same index tail rule.
